subject: physics_2
question_text: Obtain an expression for the torque on a loop placed in a uniform magnetic field. Describe the construction and working of moving coil galvanometer.

mark_split.label: Forces on the b sides cancel
The couple on the l sides

verification.note: The 1+1+1+2+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: forces i(b × B) on the two b sides act along the suspension axis and cancel; the two l sides each carry ilB and form a couple of arm b sin θ, so τ = ilB · b sin θ = iAB sin θ and τ = niAB sin θ for n turns; in the radial field of the instrument sin θ = 1, so niAB = Cθ gives i = (C/nAB)θ = Kθ — all matching the book. The book's headings print 'Movind coil galvanometer', 'equibibrium', 'defrecting' and 'carrnet pases'; these spellings are corrected here and the physics is unchanged. The first figure is drawn as a view along the axis of suspension, which is not the book's three-dimensional drawing, because the arm b sin θ of the couple can be seen directly in that view.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.
insider_note: The radial field is the line that carries the second half: it is the reason sin θ = 1 at every deflection and the reason the scale is uniform. Note the marks are not split evenly — the torque derivation carries 5 and the galvanometer 3, so a full first half with no galvanometer still earns 5.

steps.label: The coil seen along its axis
steps.margin_note: The coil seen from above, along its axis of suspension. The coil appears as a line of length b, the two l sides appear as its two ends, the normal N makes angle θ with the field B, and the two forces i l B form the couple.
steps.why: Seen this way the arm of the couple is the horizontal distance between the two force arrows, which is b sin θ — the one length the three-dimensional drawing hides.
common_mistakes: Measuring θ from the plane of the coil. It is measured from the normal to the plane.
Drawing the two forces in the same direction. They are equal and opposite and do not act along the same line.

recall.must_convey: That the coil is drawn in a uniform field with the normal at angle θ and the two equal opposite forces marked.
accept: draw the coil in the field
normal at angle theta to the field
two equal opposite forces
reject: tau equals n i A B sine theta

steps.memory_tip: One slanted line for the coil, one arrow up and one down: that is the couple.

steps.label: The coil in the field
steps.mark_note: The set-up and the angle θ
lines: Let a rectangular coil ABCD, with
AB = CD = l and AD = BC = b, carry a current
i. It is suspended in a uniform magnetic
field of induction B and is free to turn
about a vertical axis.
Let the normal to the plane of the coil make
an angle θ with the direction of the field.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the two side lengths l and b, the current i, the field B, and define θ from the NORMAL.
steps.why: θ is measured from the normal, not from the plane, so that θ = 0 means the coil faces the field squarely and feels no turning effect.
common_mistakes: Taking θ between the plane of the coil and the field, which gives cos θ instead of sin θ.
Forgetting to say the field is uniform. In a non-uniform field there is also a net force.

recall.must_convey: That a rectangular coil of sides l and b carries current i in a uniform field B, with the normal at angle θ.
accept: rectangular coil of sides l and b
uniform magnetic field of induction B
normal makes angle theta with the field
reject: forces on AD and BC cancel

steps.memory_tip: Angle from the normal, never from the plane.

steps.label: Forces on the b sides cancel
lines: The sides AD and BC, each of length b, carry
forces
These two forces are equal in size and
opposite in direction, and both act along
the vertical axis of suspension.
They therefore cancel each other and produce
no turning effect on the coil.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say why these two forces do nothing: they act along the same line, the axis of suspension.
steps.why: Two equal opposite forces along the SAME line cancel completely; it is only when their lines of action are separated that they turn the coil.
common_mistakes: Saying these forces are zero. They are not zero; they cancel.
Leaving this pair out of the answer. The examiner marks the statement that they cancel.

recall.must_convey: That the forces on the two b sides are equal and opposite along the axis of suspension and cancel.
accept: forces on AD and BC cancel
along the axis of suspension
no turning effect
reject: form a couple of arm b sine theta

steps.label: The couple on the l sides
steps.mark_note: F = ilB each, arm = b sin θ
lines: The sides AB and DC, each of length l, stay
perpendicular to the field in every position
of the coil, so each carries a force
These two forces are equal, opposite and do
not act along the same line, so they form a
couple.
The perpendicular distance between their
lines of action is the arm of the couple,
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The force on each l side, and the arm b sin θ. The sin θ enters here and nowhere else.
steps.why: Turning the coil does not change either force, only how far apart their lines of action are — which is why the whole angle dependence of the torque sits in the arm.
common_mistakes: Writing the arm as b. The arm is the perpendicular distance b sin θ, not the full side.
Writing b cos θ, which comes from measuring θ from the plane instead of the normal.

recall.must_convey: That each l side carries F = ilB and the two form a couple of arm b sin θ.
accept: force i l B on each of the two sides
they form a couple
arm is b sine theta
reject: tau equals i A B sine theta

steps.memory_tip: The forces stay the same size; only the arm changes as the coil turns.

steps.label: The torque on the coil
lines: Torque = one force × arm of the couple

lines.text: τ = (i l B)(b sin θ) = i (l b) B sin θ

lines: Since l b = A, the area of the coil,

lines.text: τ = i A B sin θ

lines: For a coil of n turns each turn contributes
the same couple, so

lines.text: τ = n i A B sin θ

lines: τ is maximum when θ = 90°, that is when the
field lies in the plane of the coil, and τ is
zero when θ = 0°.
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Show lb becoming the area A, then bring in the n turns, then the maximum and zero cases.
steps.why: Only the product lb survives, so the torque depends on the area of the loop and not on its shape — a circular loop of the same area gives the same torque.
common_mistakes: Writing τ = 2ilBb sin θ by counting both forces. A couple's torque is one force times the arm.
Dropping the n for a coil of many turns.

recall.must_convey: That τ = ilB × b sin θ = iAB sin θ, and τ = niAB sin θ for n turns.
accept: force into arm of the couple
tau equals i A B sine theta
n i A B sine theta for n turns
heard_as: n i A B sine theta

steps.memory_tip: Number of turns, current, area, field, sine of the angle — in that order.

steps.label: The moving coil galvanometer
steps.margin_note: A rectangular coil hung by a phosphor bronze wire between the concave poles N and S, with a soft iron core inside the coil and a spring at the lower end.
steps.why: The concave poles together with the soft iron core are what make the field radial, so this shape is not decoration — it is the reason the instrument reads a current directly.
common_mistakes: Drawing flat pole faces. They are concave, and with the core they make the field radial.
Leaving out the soft iron core inside the coil.

recall.must_convey: That the coil, the phosphor bronze suspension, the concave poles, the soft iron core and the spring are drawn.
accept: coil hung between the poles
phosphor bronze suspension
soft iron core and spring

steps.memory_tip: Hang the coil, curve the poles, put the core in the middle, spring at the bottom.

steps.label: Construction
lines: 1) A moving coil galvanometer has a
rectangular coil of insulated copper wire
suspended between the concave poles of a
horseshoe magnet by a phosphor bronze
wire.
2) Phosphor bronze has a high Young's modulus
and a very low rigidity modulus, so it can
be twisted easily but not stretched.
3) A soft iron cylinder is placed inside the
coil. It increases the field strength and,
with the concave poles, makes the field
radial.
4) In a radial field the field always lies in
the plane of the coil, so the deflecting
torque is n i A B at every deflection.
5) A spring at the lower end supplies the
restoring couple, and the current enters
and leaves through the suspension and the
spring.
steps.margin_note: Sixth mark. Five short numbered points. The phosphor bronze property and the radial field are the two the examiner looks for.
steps.why: Every part answers one need: the wire must twist without stretching, the core must make the field radial, and the spring must supply a restoring couple that grows with the twist. A radial field gives the coil ZERO flux, not maximum: the field lies in the plane of the coil, so the normal is at 90° to B and Φ = NBA cos 90° = 0. What it maximises is the TORQUE, τ = niAB sin θ with sin θ = 1 at every deflection — and that is what makes the scale uniform.
common_mistakes: Saying phosphor bronze has a high rigidity modulus. It is LOW, so the wire twists easily.
Saying the field is uniform. In this instrument it is radial.
Saying the radial field gives maximum flux. It gives maximum torque; the flux through the coil is zero.

recall.must_convey: The coil on a phosphor bronze suspension between concave poles, with a soft iron core making the field radial and a spring below.
accept: rectangular coil of insulated copper wire
phosphor bronze suspension twists easily
soft iron core makes the field radial
spring gives the restoring couple
reject: n i A B equals C theta

steps.memory_tip: Coil, wire, poles, core, spring — top to bottom, five parts.

steps.label: Working
steps.mark_note: Deflecting torque niAB, restoring torque Cθ
lines: When a current i passes through the coil, the
coil experiences a deflecting torque.
The field is radial, so it lies in the plane
of the coil in every position and sin θ = 1.

lines.text: deflecting torque = n i A B

lines: The coil turns and twists the suspension
wire. If the coil turns through an angle θ,
the wire sets up a restoring torque
where C is the restoring couple per unit
twist of the wire.
steps.margin_note: Seventh mark. The radial field removes sin θ from the deflecting torque; the suspension supplies a restoring torque proportional to the twist.
steps.why: Without the radial field the deflecting torque would fall as the coil turned, and equal steps of current would give smaller and smaller steps of deflection.
common_mistakes: Keeping sin θ in the deflecting torque of the instrument. The radial field makes sin θ = 1.
Writing the restoring torque as C alone. It grows with the twist, as Cθ.

recall.must_convey: That the deflecting torque is niAB because the field is radial, and the restoring torque is Cθ.
accept: deflecting torque n i A B
radial field so sine theta is one
restoring torque C theta

steps.memory_tip: Current pushes the coil round, the wire's twist pushes it back.

steps.label: Deflection proportional to current
lines: At equilibrium the deflecting torque equals
the restoring torque:

lines.text: n i A B = C θ
i = (C / n A B) θ = K θ
i ∝ θ,   K = C / n A B

lines: K is called the galvanometer constant.
The current is directly proportional to the
deflection, so the instrument has a uniform
scale.
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Equate the two torques, make i the subject, and finish with the statement that the scale is uniform.
steps.why: Every quantity in K is fixed by the construction, so once the instrument is built the deflection reads the current on a scale of equal divisions.
common_mistakes: Writing θ ∝ 1/i. The deflection grows with the current.
Leaving out the constant K or its expression C/nAB.

recall.must_convey: That niAB = Cθ gives i = (C/nAB)θ = Kθ, so the current is proportional to the deflection.
accept: n i A B equals C theta
i equals K theta
K is C by n A B
uniform scale

steps.memory_tip: Set the two torques equal and the current falls out as a straight multiple of the turn.
